title: Certificates of Deposit: Penalties Booked at a Rate or Day Count Other Than the Term's
content:
For Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit, an early withdrawal penalty is only as good as the figures it was booked with. This page covers the credit-back owed when a penalty on a certificate was charged at a rate, or for a number of penalty days, other than those the certificate terms fix for the term in which the withdrawal was taken.

## What the bank owes

A penalty booked with a rate or a penalty-day figure that departs from the terms of its term was charged in breach of those terms, and it is credited back to the certificate as a bank error. The credit is owed whether or not the owner raises it.

The effect the owner sees is a credit entry in the certificate's activity that cancels the penalty entry, and a principal balance that is higher by the credited sum from that moment.

## Carrying out the credit-back

The credit-back is an agent action performed with `reverse_penalty_error_2ccc5de3`. The tool is hidden until the agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`; once unlocked, the agent calls it through `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, supplying the arguments below.

### What the tool does

It posts one penalty reversal entry on the certificate, dated the current day, linked to the penalty entry being reversed and marked with the adjustment reason `bank_error`. The credited sum joins the certificate's principal balance straight away. Nothing else about the certificate changes.

### Arguments

| Argument | What it identifies or carries | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `certificate_id` | The certificate bearing the penalty, as the certificate lookup for the customer returns it | Reference number |
| `source_item_id` | The penalty entry being credited back, as the certificate activity lookup returns it | Entry reference number |
| `amount` | The sum credited back to principal | USD with 2 decimal places, positive, rounded half-up to the cent |

The tool accepts the figures it is given; it does not work out the credit itself.

### What comes back

A successful call returns a receipt listing `reversal_id` (the reference of the new reversal entry), `certificate_id`, `source_item_id`, `amount`, `posted_date` (the current day, as YYYY-MM-DD) and `principal_balance` (the certificate's new principal, 2 decimal places). A receipt that carries a `reversal_id` confirms the credit is posted.

## Basis Q&A

**Does the owner have to ask for this credit?** No. The credit is due on the strength of the certificate's own records.
